summary.intent: Clean up a change set in the ask_soony project by reverting a dotenv load that happened at import time, verifying the tests pass, and amending the previous commit.
summary.outcome: A single Bash step reverted the import-time dotenv load, ran the tests twice, and amended the commit. The change touched .env.example, api.py, background.py, replies.py, teams.py and tests/test_teams.py. The transcript does not show test output, so the results are unconfirmed.

repo: Configuration loading in ask_soony should not happen at module import time; the dotenv load was reverted from import scope.
The change set spans the API, background, replies and teams modules plus .env.example, so environment configuration is likely shared across several modules.
tests/test_teams.py covers the teams module and was modified alongside the source changes.
workflow: Running tests twice before amending suggests a check for flakiness or order-dependence before rewriting history.
Amending the commit instead of creating a new one keeps the change set as a single logical commit.

friction: The transcript has no test output, so it is unclear whether both test runs passed.
Import-time side effects (dotenv loading) had to be backed out, suggesting an earlier approach caused problems.
open_items: Decide where dotenv loading should happen instead, for example an explicit entry point or app startup, if it is still needed.
Confirm .env.example matches the environment variables the modules actually read.
